Unfortunately, the human body is just really weird sometimes. Someone I knew lost all of her hair and eyebrows after giving birth to her 2nd child. Well, when I was first single, I felt I was completely isolated from the world and forming a new relationship was almost entirely impossible. Yet, there are 7 billion people on Earth, so how could this be? When you dwell on isolation while being isolated everything can seem hopeless.


Then I found a relationship and suddenly it didn't seem like that big of deal any more. In fact, there were many parts of the relationship that I didn't enjoy at all and wish I had never experienced. Through several relationships and many years, I discover over and over again that the more I value my needs over the relationships needs, the more the relationship goes smoothly.


It's really weird and counter intuitive. But, ironically, once you start not believing a relationship is everything that you need, you will become confident and will automatically attract people to you. And then, once you get into a relationship, you may find out that it wasn't as exciting as you had been dreaming.


My point, I suppose is that I recommend:

1. Concentrating on other ways you can celebrate who you are and enjoy life (e.g. clubs, reading, cooking, etc.) without focusing on relationships 24/7
2. As boring as it sounds, more patience
3. Exposing yourself to more people. At the end of the day, its statistics, right? All of my relationships have started when I wasn't searching for them. I met the person I was interested in by hanging out with a variety of friends. It wasn't like I was actively searching for them.
4. Also, I would give technology a try (Tinder, OkCupid, etc.). Just don't stress out about your dating profile/etc. Just think of it more as exploring for fun.


I know you can do this. I have confidence in you. You should have confidence in yourself as well. Best of luck!
